The petitioners are the accused Nos.1 to 3 in Crime No.172/2023 registered by Kodungallur Police alleging the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420 and 468 read with Section 34 of IPC.
2.
The defacto complainant is the brother of the 1 st petitioner.
The 2nd and 3rd petitioners are the wife and son of the 1 st petitioner.
The allegation against the petitioners is that, the accused Nos.1 to 3 were entrusted with the ATM card, credit card and the cheque of the father of the 1st petitioner and the defacto complainant.
It is alleged that, using the cheques of the father, the petitioners have withdrawn the money from the account of the father and misappropriated the same.
It is also alleged that even after the death of the father on 06.11.2022, the petitioners have withdrawn the amounts using the ATM Card of the father.

In such circumstances, a private complaint was submitted by the defacto complainant which was referred for investigation by the BAIL APPL. NO.
1705 OF 2023 jurisdictional court to the Police.
Thereupon the crime was registered.
This application for anticipatory bail is submitted by the petitioners, as they apprehend arrest.

3. Heard Sri. M.Shaju Purushothaman, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, Sri.C.N.
Prabhakaran, learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the State and Sri.Rajit, learned counsel appearing for the defacto complainant who is impleaded as additional 2nd respondent.
4.
The learned counsel for the petitioners submits the petitioners were falsely implicated in the said case.
According to them, the father was being looked after by the petitioners and the amounts withdrawn from the account of the father was being utilized for his treatment.
As regards the withdrawal of the amounts using the ATM card after death of the father, it was pointed out that, the same was utilized for the purpose of funeral expenses of the father.
According to him, the defacto complainant was making unsustainable allegations against the petitioners.
The petitioners are BAIL APPL. NO. 1705 OF 2023 willing to cooperate with the investigation and are ready to abide by any conditions imposed by this Court.
5. On the other hand, the learned Public Prosecutor as well as the learned counsel appearing for the defacto complainant stoutly opposes the application for bail.

The counsel for the defacto complainant points out that, the petitioners had withdrawn huge amounts totaling to Rs.45 lakhs from the account of the father of the petitioners, by forging his signature in the cheques.
It is pointed out that even after his death the withdrawal continued.
The learned Public Prosecutor Faisal C.H vs State Of Kerala on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114627379/

sentences.text: 2 submits that, the investigation in the matter is in progress.
However, with respect to the allegation regarding forgery it was submitted that, as of now no materials are available.
6. I have gone through the records and heard the contentions raised by all the parties concerned.
From the materials placed on record, it is evident that this is a dispute between siblings.
Even though it is alleged that, the petitioners have withdrawn the amounts by committing forgery, as of now there are BAIL APPL. NO. 1705 OF 2023 no materials available on record.
However, it is a matter for investigation.
Therefore, I am not going deep into same.

But considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the relationship between the deceased and the petitioners as well as the defacto complainant, I am of the view that, the custodial interrogation of the petitioners may not be necessary.
Interest of justice would be served, if the cooperation of the petitioners with the investigation is ensured.

In such circumstances, this application is disposed of with the following directions:
i) The petitioners shall surrender before the Investigating Officer, within a period of two weeks from today, for subjecting themselves to interrogation.
ii) After interrogation, the petitioners shall be released on bail on the very same day of surrender upon the petitioners executing a bond for Rs 1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) each with two sureties each for the like sum, to the satisfaction of the BAIL APPL. NO. 1705 OF 2023 Investigating Officer.
iii) The petitioners shall fully co-operate with the investigation, including subjecting themselves to the deemed police custody for the purpose of recovery, if any, as and when demanded.
iv) The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer between 10.00 a.m and 11.00 a.m every Saturday until the filing of the final report.
v) The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.
vi) The petitioners shall not commit any offence of similar nature while on bail.

vii) The petitioners shall not make any attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses, directly or through any other person, or in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
viii) The petitioners shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the Jurisdictional Court.
BAIL APPL. NO. 1705 OF 2023

In case of violation of any of the above conditions, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider the application for cancellation of bail, if any, and pass Faisal C.H vs State Of Kerala on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114627379/
